collectorBoundaryIssue.explanation: An intentional unauthenticated check completed logging just after measurement start. All 250 measured client requests returned 200, with 250 corresponding authenticated events. Raw mismatch/server-event flags are retained, but do not represent an application failure. The phase also stopped independently on sustained host steal. Functional follow-up separates the expected 401 checks and waits before measurement.

changes: Same gzip MIME types, compression level and minimum size as production.
Hashed/static assets receive production cache policy; index and SPA fallback use no-cache.
The staging environment header and IP allowlist behavior remain in place.
localCorrection.validation: Real local Nginx before/after HTTP probes, no external network or published ports; JS, CSS and MJS gzip decompression equals the synthetic fixture; HTML/SPA cache policies verified. Synthetic byte reduction is not a measurement of real application bundle reduction.

cpuProfileObservation: In one separate point-summary request after TTL expiration, date conversion addDate was no longer in the top-35 self-sample list. Garbage collection (231/1264 samples) and monthly calculation functions remained visible. The truncated list and unstable host do not establish an exact CPU gain.
browserHarnessSetupIssueResolved: Initial browser probes selected the default roles cost tab; the corrected URL selects cost=rates. Both intended authenticated surfaces then loaded with 200 API responses and no measured JS/network errors. Logout may produce a later expected auth/me 401 after the measured navigation window.
limitations: Load attempts planned 100 requests per route but stopped after 18 requests at 2/s and 250 at 1/s due five consecutive host-steal samples >=50%. No route/profile/mode completed a 100-sample cohort; no p95 is reported.
Functional follow-up uses one measured request per route/mode and an initial warmup pass. It does not replace load acceptance.
Only the dedicated staging administrator was tested remotely. No viewer, permission-edit, external business-write or cross-session freshness acceptance in this round.

Controlled API tests use temporary same-image HTTP instances with jobs disabled, pool8, 1.5CPU/2GiB. Existing staging API and its background jobs remained running. This does not exactly reproduce production worker topology.
API cohort timings use internal Docker HTTP; separate browser probes use public HTTPS and existing staging configuration.
Sequential phases have differing host load. Reduced-rate results cannot be used as a like-for-like percentage comparison with earlier 2/s measurements.
Browser login is five local Chromium navigations with viewport390x844, 200000B/s,150ms latency,4x CPU,cache disabled and reused connections; not real-user data.

Authenticated browser checks include normal auth/session/access bookkeeping and main-element presence, API success and numeric content marks; no visual interaction or financial edits. The monthly screen has no content-visible instrumentation sample.
CPU profiling is a single extra point-summary request outside measured cohorts, after cache TTL; statistical truncated self samples, not exact CPU milliseconds.
No code/configuration deployment, restart, quota adjustment, backup, retention or business edit was performed on the VPS.
nextSteps: Publish the local Nginx staging configuration and recreate only staging nginx so the bind-mounted configuration is refreshed.
Repeat the five simulated login navigations and verify gzip/cache response headers after deployment.
Use the recorded high-steal and resting-host series with the hosting provider to investigate vCPU availability.
Complete comparable >=100-request route/profile cohorts and production 24-hour/seven-day observation when infrastructure permits.
